senses.gloss: to split, break, esp. (v. בָּצַע) to break bread and say grace.
units: <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 29b:3">R. Hash. 29ᵇ</cite> <he>לא יִפְרוֹס אדם פרוסה וכ׳</he> a person should not break bread and say grace for his guests, unless he dines with them <he>אבל פּוֹרֵס הוא לבניו וכ׳</he> but he may do so for his children and his household in order to train them in religious practice.

<cite ref="Pesachim 37a">Pes. 37ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Menachot 78b:12">Men. 78ᵇ</cite> (expl. <he>מצה הינא</he>) <he>כל שפּוֹרְסָהּ ואין וכ׳</he> when he breaks it apart, and no cords (of unbaked dough) can be drawn out of it; a. e.—Part. pass. <cite ref="Q01700"><he>פָּרוּס</he></cite>; f. <cite ref="Q01711"><he>פְּרוּסָה</he></cite>; pl. <he>פְּרוּסִים</he>, <he>פְּרוּסִין</he>; <he>פְּרוּסוֹת</he>.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 34:11">Lev. R. s. 34</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Q01913"><he>פָּרֹס</he></cite>, <cite ref="Isaiah 58:7">Is. LVIII, 7</cite>) <he>הלא תִפְרוֹשׂ … פָרוּס כבר היא פ׳ וכ׳</he> it does not read, ‘behold, thou shalt break’, but, ‘behold broken’; it (thy bread) is broken for thee, for from the beginning of the year it is decreed &c.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 1:2:6">Y. Dem. I, 21ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>בפ׳</he> when it is a broken piece of an eatable, opp. <he>שלם</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:1:25">Y. Ber. VI, 10ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>פ׳ של חטים</he> (sub. <cite ref="Q02110"><he>פת</he></cite>) a broken loaf of wheat bread; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="Q01701"><he>פְּרוּס</he></cite>, <cite ref="Q01711"><he>פְּרוּסָה</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: (cmp. פָּרַץ) to break through; part. pass. as ab. open, plain.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 5:4">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. V, 4</cite>, v. <cite ref="O00226"><he>סַוָּאר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 3:3">Meg. III, 3</cite> (<cite ref="Megillah 28a:22">28ᵃ</cite>) <he>ואין פּוֹרְשִׂין לתוכו מצודות</he> nor dare you spread traps leading into it (the synagogue in ruins).
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 3:4">Yoma III, 4</cite> <he>פָּרְסוּ סדין וכ׳</he> (Y. ed. <he>פָּרְשׂוּ</he>), v. <cite ref="O00185"><he>סָדִין</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 11:2">Num. R. s. 11</cite> <he>הכהנים פּוֹרְשִׂים את כפיהם</he> the priests spread their hands (when blessing).
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 42">Ex. R. s. 42</cite> <he>אחז … ופ׳ הקב״ה וכ׳</he> he (Moses) took hold of the divine throne, and the Lord spread his cloak over him.

<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 42">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <he>פּ֗ר̇ש̇ז̇</he>, <cite ref="Job 26:9">Job XXVI, 9</cite>) <he>פ̇</he>' <he>ר̇חום ש̇די ז̇יו וכ׳</he> the Merciful Almighty spread the splendor of his cloud over him; <cite ref="Job 26:9">ib.</cite> s. 41 <he>פ׳ והגין עליו הקב״ה</he> the Lord spread (his cloak) over him and protected him; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 5">Deut. R. s. 5</cite> <he>היה פוֹרֵשׂ דיאטגמא וכ׳</he> (not <he>דאטגמא</he>) he spread (published) a decree wherever he conquered &c.—Part. pass. as ab.

Ab. III, 16, v. מְצוּדָה; a. e.—פ׳ על שמע (interch. with פ׳ את שמע) to spread a cloak over the head for the recitation of the prayers preceding the Shmʿa (Ḳaddish and Bar’khu), esp. to recite the prayers &c. for the benefit of those who have come too late for the regular service (cmp.
<cite ref="Berakhot 51a:20">Ber. 51ᵃ</cite> <he>פריס סודרא</he>, quot. in <cite ref="Q01909">next w.</cite>).

Meg. IV, 3 (23ᵇ) אין פורסין על שמע וכ׳ (Mish. ed. את; Mish. Pes. פורשין, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 90) the prayers for the Shmʿa are not read aloud … with less than two persons; [Rashi: to divide the Sh’ma (v. supra), i.e. to read parts of the prayers preceding the Shmʿa;] Y. ib. IV, 75ᵃ bot. פורסין את שמע. Ib. IV, 5 המפטיר … פורס וכ׳, v. פָּטַר. Ib. 6.

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 23:4">Lev. R. s. 23</cite> <he>א״ל פְּרוֹס על שמע פ׳</he> they said to him, recite the prayers for the Shmʿa; he did; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:2:4">Cant. R. to II, 2</cite> (mixed dict.) <he>פְּרוֹס לן את שמע פרוס לון</he> (read: <cite ref="Q01909"><he>פָּרֵיס</he></cite>); a. fr.
<cite ref="Mishnah Tevul Yom 3:1">T’bul Yom III, 1</cite>, v. <cite ref="P01342"><he>עָרָה</he> II</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 7:7">B. Mets. VII, 7</cite> <he>נִתְפָּרְסוּ עיגוליו</he> if his fig cakes were broken; a. e.

senses.gloss: to assign, give a share, a present.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 74">Gen. R. s. 74</cite> end <he>ולא היו מַפְרִיסִים וכ׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>מפרינים</he>) they endowed only with their mouth, v. <cite ref="Q01879"><he>פָּרַן</he></cite>. Yalk. ib. 22 <he>מַפְרִיס והולך</he>, v. <cite ref="Q02041"><he>פְּרָת</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: (denom. of פַּרְסָה) to part the foot, to have a parted hoof. Sifra Sh’mini, ch. V, Par. 4 משוסע, חזיר מפריס the swine parts its foot and is cloven-footed.
units: <cite ref="Chullin 59a:14">Ḥull. 59ᵃ</cite> <he>אין לך דבר שמפריס פרסה וכ׳</he> there is no animal that parts its foot and yet is unclean, except swine; a. e.—

Ib. 51ᵇ ה׳ ע״ג קרקע the animal, after its fall, in attempting to rise made an impression of its parted feet on the ground (an evidence of its spine’s being unaffected).—Trnsf. to show the cloven foot (like swine, as if saying, ‘I am clean’, v.
Lev. R. s. 13, end), to pretend piety.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 22:13">Gen. R. s. 22</cite> <he>יצא כמפריס וכמרמה וכ׳</he> (some ed. <he>מפרים</he>, corr. acc.) he went forth like a hypocrite and as one deceiving his Creator; (Yalk. ib. 38; <cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 10:5">Lev. R. s. 10</cite> <he>כמַעֲרִים</he>, v. <cite ref="P01391"><he>עָרַם</he> II</cite>).

<cite ref="Bekhorot 44a:15">Bekh. 44ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Exodus 40:19">Ex. XL, 19</cite>) <he>רבינו פֵּירְשׂוֹ</he> Moses our teacher spread it (hence he must have been ten cubits high); <cite ref="Shabbat 92a:7">Sabb. 92ᵃ</cite> <he>פרשו</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 372:1">Yalk. Ex. 372</cite>; a. e.

senses.gloss: to put a wrap on, only in פֵּירְסָה נדה she became menstruous.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 2a">Keth. 2ᵃ</cite>.
